# Invite-ready free Scope 1 beta plan

Date: 2026-09-24. Task: `SCOPE1-FREE-BETA-PLAN-20260924`. Owner: CPO planner `/root/scope1_beta_plan`; sponsor, integration owner and shared-record owner: root coordinator. Requested route: `gpt-5.6-sol` / `medium`; observed model and effort are unknown. Role prompt SHA-256: `fe5237292aafa6fe307801d3d9d07414110d11dc6ecd7812ee52ed77feacb2e6`.

This plan defines the earliest honest invitation-ready free Scope 1 beta for two or three known companies. It does not authorize implementation before the accepted M78 integration is merged, invite anyone, approve a source or method, decide a company's legal obligations, establish customer-complete Scope 1, launch a paid product, or provide external assurance.

## Product decision

The next customer-facing target is **M80: a free, invitation-only Scope 1 drafting beta**. The beta helps a known company create a tenant, declare its reporting boundary, upload real evidence, calculate only released supported profiles, see named gaps, download a draft report and send feedback. Neuvetra owns calculation validation and source traceability. A beta user supplies company facts and evidence; the user is never asked to verify Neuvetra's factors, formulas, units, rounding or totals.

Invitation readiness is a narrower release than complete customer Scope 1. A company may receive an invitation when the secured journey and supported calculations have passed the gates below. Its report remains a **draft known-source subtotal** until its entity/source census and evidence are complete and independently reviewed. A beta invitation does not mean the company has a complete inventory, an SB 253 filing, a compliance determination, a paid entitlement or an assurance opinion.

The earliest supported calculation envelope is deliberately concrete, but it is not an assumed industry cohort:

- reporting period: calendar year 2025, `2025-01-01` through `2025-12-31`;
- organization: one parent with wholly controlled U.S. operations using the operational-control approach, no joint ventures, acquisitions, disposals or ownership changes during the year;
- organizational shape: a complete entity and location census, including controlled operations outside California when applicable, that confirms no joint ventures, acquisitions, disposals or ownership changes during the year;
- supported activity families: supplied HHV MMBtu stationary natural gas; directly metered U.S. gallons of fossil Distillate No. 2 for an emergency generator; owned or controlled on-road medium/heavy fossil-diesel vehicles in model years 2007–2022 with both gallons and actual miles; and stable serviced equipment using HFC-134a, HFC-227ea or whole-blend R-410A under the current bounded event method; and
- unsupported at beta entry: process emissions, biomass, renewable diesel, gasoline, propane/LPG, non-road equipment, shared-meter or intercompany allocation, unsupported vehicle classes/model years, refrigerant stock/retrofit/acquisition/disposal methods, unknown gases, offsets/credits and any other source family without an explicit release row.

No industry is assumed. Before invitation approval, a short eligibility intake asks for the boundary approach, reporting year, entities and locations; stationary and mobile fuels; owned/controlled vehicles; refrigerants and fire-suppression gases; process emissions; direct releases; and available evidence. It maps each disclosed source to `supported candidate`, `unsupported`, `uncertain` or `not applicable pending evidence`. A manufacturing, beauty, retail, logistics or other company is eligible only to the extent its actual census fits the released envelope. A possible introduction through a former employer or an Aveda supply-chain or demand contact is a prospect, not evidence of fit, customer status or permission to contact.

The source census, not marketing copy or industry label, decides fit. A company with an unsupported or uncertain applicable source can still use the beta to organize evidence and receive a draft with a named blocker, but Neuvetra must not present a complete company total. An evidence-backed not-applicable decision or zero requires the exact census and reviewer basis; the product must not infer either from silence.

The board must select the two or three named known companies and authorize the exact recipient list and evidence-processing boundary. Until then, `Beta company 1`, `Beta company 2` and optional `Beta company 3` are selection slots, not customers or active invitations.

## M79 gates required for M80 numbers

M79 preparation already accounts for four profiles and twelve gas/factor rows. Its bounded numerical dossier passed exact arithmetic compatibility for the current candidate engines. The seven retained source artifacts and all 21 classified intended uses remain on Neuvetra product-release hold. M80 may consume no calculation profile until all relevant release gates below are satisfied on one frozen version.

| M79 gate | Evidence required before M80 may display that profile's number | Decision owner | Failure behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact source and method identity | Retained bytes, edition/date, locator, activity unit/heat basis, gas rows, displayed precision, GWP/blend rule, estimate/zero rule, effective period and supersession rule match the accepted inventory. | Accounting validator with source/domain researcher; independent source review | Block the affected profile and name the missing or conflicting item. |
| Numerical compatibility | Independent deterministic re-derivation covers representative, boundary and half-even cases; exact engine and server totals match; unrounded contributions aggregate once. | Independent accounting reviewer, separate from implementation | Show no calculated value from the affected profile. Do not ask the beta user to adjudicate it. |
| Domain applicability | A qualified reviewer records `approved`, `blocked` or `requires further review` for the exact factor route, unit/heat basis, GWP policy, blend treatment, estimation/zero rule, 2025 period and supported activity facts. | Qualified accounting/domain reviewer | Keep the profile unreleased; collect evidence only and show the blocker. |
| Intended-use rights | A written, source-specific decision separately covers numerical calculation/derived values and the exact citations or excerpts planned for customer reports. Hosted fulltext/RAG remains separately held unless explicitly approved. | Neuvetra rights owner; qualified counsel only where the classified act and legal basis require interpretation | Use no held artifact for the undecided act. Permission or a license is sought only if the recorded source/use analysis says it is needed. |
| Immutable release decision | An authorized release record binds exact methods, factors, source artifacts, rights/domain decisions, effective dates, exclusions and supersession. Caller flags and hashes cannot grant eligibility. | Authorized release owner after the preceding reviews | `releaseEligible=false`; preserve old candidate/report bytes. |
| Runtime enforcement | API and browser refuse missing, blocked, expired, incompatible, corrupt or superseded releases while retaining named gaps and any separately eligible subtotal. Tenant authorization remains independent of public method metadata. | One backend/data implementation writer; security review; independent QA | Fail closed without losing uploaded evidence or implying zero. |

These gates do not assume that every numerical fact requires a license, that public availability grants permission, or that beta status creates a blanket exemption. Individual facts, independently expressed methods and calculated outputs must be classified separately from copied source expression, table arrangement, screenshots, excerpts and fulltext storage. The written decision controls only the exact act it analyzes.

M79 is sufficient for M80 only when every profile that will produce a number in the rehearsal has an approved release record and the runtime enforces it. M79 may truthfully finish with other profiles blocked. The admitted company's applicable source census must then either stay entirely within the released subset or make the draft explicitly incomplete.

## M80 user journey and acceptance

M80 passes only on one frozen candidate after the accepted M78 integration is merged and the relevant M79 release records are frozen.

### Observed experience to refine

The coordinator's read-only September 24 inspection found a preserved sign-in and synthetic workspace with 13 peer Workspace views, including five electricity/history views alongside Scope 1. It correctly exposed private-staging and synthetic-company limits, but the Scope 1 path is not yet the focused beta journey: the register presents 104 findings and dense source identifiers without enough prioritization or context. These are current UI observations, not customer evidence or M80 acceptance.

M80 therefore adds a Scope 1-focused onboarding route and navigation, an eligibility intake, a supported-source chooser, contextual units and evidence prompts, and a short prioritized action list. Findings are grouped as `blocks calculation`, `blocks completeness`, `needs review` or `informational`, with the next action and affected source in plain language. The full audit detail remains available. Synthetic/private-staging labels are replaced only for an authorized real-company tenant after its real-data gates pass; they are never removed as a cosmetic shortcut.

### 1. Refined landing and beta message

The public landing page explains the offered job in plain language: “Organize your 2025 Scope 1 evidence, calculate supported sources and see what is still missing.” It identifies the beta as free, invitation-only and draft. It states the supported source envelope and examples of unsupported activities before sign-up, without presenting an industry as already supported.

The page and application must not claim industry-wide coverage, SB 253 applicability for the visitor, compliance, filing readiness, audit readiness, verification, certification, assurance, guaranteed accuracy or a complete inventory. It may say that supported calculations are deterministic, versioned, source-traceable and independently checked when the exact release evidence supports those statements. “Free beta” must not imply future pricing, entitlement or service terms that have not been approved.

Acceptance evidence: independent content review of desktop and mobile renderings; all primary calls to action lead to invitation entry or sign-in; support, privacy and draft-status language are reachable; unsupported examples are visible before evidence upload.

### 2. Invitation, sign-in and company setup

Only a single-use, expiring invitation bound to one approved recipient and intended company can create or join the tenant. Sign-in, invitation redemption, tenant membership, role enforcement and logout are server-authorized. A recipient cannot enumerate, redeem or access another company's invitation, setup, evidence, calculation or report.

Setup begins with the eligibility intake and records the exact legal company name, 2025 reporting period, operational-control choice, entities, facilities, locations, ownership/control facts, source census and process-emissions/direct-release screen. A supported-source chooser shows only profiles backed by effective release records and explains the required unit and evidence. Users can save and resume. Unsupported, missing or conflicting facts remain named findings and cannot silently become not applicable.

Acceptance evidence: authorized redemption and resume work; expired, reused, wrong-recipient and cross-tenant attempts fail; correction history is retained; unsupported sources are flagged before document-heavy onboarding; incomplete setup cannot show a complete-company label.

### 3. Real document and activity intake

The beta accepts only predeclared formats and size limits needed for the supported profiles, with malware/type/size checks, tenant-scoped encrypted storage, least-privilege retrieval, immutable provenance and a clear delete/retention path. At minimum, the rehearsed bundle includes entity/facility records plus applicable gas bills or meter summaries, diesel fuel records, vehicle register and mileage evidence, equipment register and service records, and a process-screen attestation.

Each document is linked to company, reporting year, facility/source, evidence type, period and uploader. Structured values extracted or entered from a document remain proposals until the user confirms the transcription and Neuvetra validates units, periods and duplicates. The original stays available to authorized reviewers. Unsupported formats or ambiguous evidence remain visible and do not feed a calculation.

Acceptance evidence: upload, validation, correction, duplicate detection, authorized download and deletion/retention behavior pass with safe representative documents; malicious, oversized, cross-tenant and unsupported inputs fail without exposure or partial calculation.

### 4. Supported intake, evidence and calculation

The application requests only the facts needed by the selected released profiles and explains units with examples. It checks reporting period, fuel/gas identity, HHV basis, vehicle class/model year, gallons plus miles, equipment/gas/event stability and evidence coverage before calculation. The server alone chooses an eligible effective release and performs decimal arithmetic. The UI never accepts a user-supplied factor, GWP, release flag or calculated total as authority.

For every displayed result, a reviewer can trace company → entity → facility → source → activity/evidence → unit conversion → factor/GWP locator → exact method/release version → gas-level result → subtotal. Input controls explain the unit in context and identify acceptable evidence. Missing evidence, conflicting periods, duplicates, unsupported facts, mixed-zero mobile inputs and incomplete service history block the affected result. Previously generated drafts remain immutable after correction or supersession.

Acceptance evidence: independent accounting fixtures reproduce every released profile used in the rehearsal; boundary and corruption cases fail closed; source-to-report trace replay matches exact totals; no beta-user judgment is part of numerical acceptance.

### 5. Draft report and workpaper package

The report and working inventory clearly separate and prioritize:

- supported calculated emissions by gas, source, facility and company subtotal;
- estimates and their exact method/uncertainty statement;
- evidence-backed zero or not-applicable findings;
- missing, conflicting and unsupported items;
- method/factor/source versions and usable citations; and
- review status, corrections and unresolved findings.

The main workspace presents a short ordered queue: calculation blockers first, then completeness blockers, then review items. Human-readable source names lead; dense identifiers remain in trace details and exports. Scope 2/electricity/history views remain available where already preserved, but they do not compete with the invited user's Scope 1 onboarding path or imply that Scope 2 is part of this beta.

The title is `2025 Scope 1 draft — known-source subtotal` until every completeness gate for that company/year passes. The report says it is not a filing, compliance determination, verification or assurance opinion. A download includes the readable draft and a machine-readable trace package without exposing another tenant or held source content.

Acceptance evidence: independent report review reconciles every displayed number to the released calculation record, confirms named gaps survive export, and verifies that unsupported items cannot be hidden by a user or administrator.

### 6. Feedback and support

Each invited user can report a problem from the relevant setup, evidence, calculation or report context without attaching source documents by default. The receipt identifies the company, page, report version and safe diagnostic reference. The UI provides the approved support channel, expected support scope and a way to report privacy/security concerns. Support access to customer evidence requires an authorized role and is audited.

Acceptance evidence: feedback submission, acknowledgement, triage ownership, safe diagnostics and access audit work in rehearsal; the product does not promise response times or services that have not been approved.

### 7. Exact end-to-end rehearsal

A fresh invited test user completes one exact representative journey: invitation → sign-in → company/year setup → entity/facility/source census → document upload → transcription confirmation → deterministic calculation → draft review → correction → regenerated draft → download → feedback → sign-out → signed-in revisit. A second tenant runs an overlapping journey to challenge isolation. Backup/recovery and restart/revisit preserve both tenants, immutable old drafts and audit history.

The rehearsal bundle includes at least one released calculated profile, one named missing item, one unsupported item and one correction. Independent accounting checks all numbers; security checks identity, authorization and document isolation; product QA checks claims, accessibility, mobile/desktop usability and error recovery. The exact hosted version and release records are frozen before the rehearsal. A failed check blocks invitation readiness.

### 8. Invitation readiness decision

The Head of QA issues an independent verdict on the frozen candidate after accounting, security and product reviews. CPO confirms the landing and in-product claims. The coordinator verifies the exact deployment, recovery evidence, support ownership and approved invite package.

No invitation is sent until the board or delegated commercial owner approves the exact named companies, recipient addresses, reporting year, processing boundary and final invitation text. Authorization to build or rehearse the beta is not authorization to contact recipients.

## Critical path and role assignments

No implementation starts until root confirms the accepted M78 integration is merged. Planning, review preparation and company-selection questions may proceed without touching Git, hosts or customer systems.

| Order | Bounded assignment and one writer | Exit evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | **CPO writer:** freeze the M80 supported envelope, eligibility intake, landing claims, Scope 1 navigation, supported-source chooser, prioritized findings, setup fields, report labels and unsupported cases; incorporate the root's website inspection. | Accepted product contract and screen-level claim matrix. |
| 2 | **Accounting/source writer:** convert accepted M79 preparation into row-level domain, rights and release-decision packets for only the profiles proposed for the rehearsal. Independent accounting/source reviewers do not author the release. | Explicit approved/blocked decisions; independently checked deterministic fixtures; no unresolved use hidden. |
| 3 | **CTO/data design writer:** define tenant/company/year, invitation, document, provenance, release, calculation, report and feedback boundaries against the exact merged M78 version. | Reviewed design with migration, rollback, data-retention and recovery contract. |
| 4 | **Backend/data implementation writer:** implement server authorization, invitation redemption, company setup, real-document controls, released-profile intake/calculation, draft export and immutable history. | Focused API/database/security checks and reproducible trace package. |
| 5 | **Frontend implementation writer:** refine the landing and complete invitation, setup, evidence, result, gap, report and feedback experiences against the accepted contract. | Desktop/mobile/keyboard/error-state evidence; no unsupported claims. |
| 6 | **Security/reliability reviewer:** independently test identity, invitations, tenant isolation, document handling, audit, restart and recovery on the integrated candidate. | Exact-version security and recovery verdict with findings resolved or blocking. |
| 7 | **Accounting reviewer and QA lead:** independently rederive every displayed number, challenge complete/zero/not-applicable states, then run the exact two-tenant end-to-end rehearsal. | Frozen acceptance receipt; named remaining limits; invitation-ready or blocked verdict. |
| 8 | **Commercial-operations writer:** prepare the exact invite package, onboarding checklist, support owner, feedback triage and stop/escalation procedure. | Reviewable package awaiting recipient authorization; no invitation sent. |

Coupled backend/database changes stay with one implementation writer. Frontend work begins from the frozen product/API contract and does not independently invent accounting state. Reviewers use fresh or independent contexts and review exact frozen artifacts; authors cannot be sole release reviewers.

## Exact blockers and decisions

Internal work can proceed through preparation, implementation and rehearsal once M78 merge is confirmed. The following are genuine external or qualified-review dependencies:

1. **Company and recipient selection:** the board or delegated commercial owner names two or three known companies after the eligibility intake, the exact 2025 legal/reporting boundary to explore, and authorized recipient addresses. No specific company, industry cohort or invitation exists today, and no invitation may be sent before that decision.
2. **Customer data authorization:** each company authorizes the exact users, 2025 evidence types, retention/deletion terms and approved tenant/provider boundary before real documents are uploaded. Customer evidence is not needed for synthetic rehearsal.
3. **Qualified accounting/domain decisions:** a qualified reviewer approves or blocks each exact released profile and later reviews company boundary, source census, estimates, zeros/not-applicable findings and the resulting draft. Beta users do not perform this QA.
4. **Source/use rights decision:** Neuvetra's rights owner records the legal basis for each exact numerical, report/excerpt and any corpus act. Qualified counsel is needed only for unresolved interpretation or when the selected act/basis requires it. A purchase or permission request requires its own authorization.
5. **Invite authorization:** after independent readiness acceptance, an authorized owner approves the exact recipients and message. This is separate from technical release.

No invented calendar estimate is attached to these dependencies. If a release decision or company fact is blocked, the plan narrows the rehearsed released subset or produces a draft with an explicit blocker; it never changes the method, hides the source or turns unknown into zero to meet a date.

## Release boundaries

| State | What it establishes | What remains false |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M79 accepted release decision | Exact approved or blocked method/source/use rows and fail-closed eligibility for a bounded profile. | Customer evidence, invitation readiness, complete company Scope 1, filing/compliance and assurance. |
| M80 invitation-ready free beta | Secure real-document drafting journey, independently verified released-profile numbers, truthful gaps, recovery/support rehearsal and an approved invitation package. | Invitation sent, complete customer Scope 1, paid launch, SB 253 filing readiness, legal applicability determination and external assurance. |
| Invited company beta | Authorized recipients may prepare a 2025 draft inside the approved data boundary. | A complete or accepted inventory and any assurance opinion. |
| Customer-complete Scope 1 | Exact company/year boundary and source census, released applicable methods, reconciled evidence, qualified review and operational acceptance all pass. | Scope 2, Scope 3, complete corporate SB 253 MVP, paid commercial launch and external assurance unless separately completed. |
| Paid launch / assurance | Separate commercial, legal, operational and independent-provider decisions. | Never inferred from beta participation or internal review. |

## Completion statement

M80 is complete only when a frozen hosted candidate lets an independently reviewed invited test user move from onboarding through real-document-shaped evidence to a reproducible draft report, with independently verified supported numbers and visible missing/unsupported items; a second tenant proves isolation; restart/recovery preserves history; the landing and product make only supported claims; support is owned; and the exact invitation package is ready for authorized recipients. The milestone may finish as technically invitation-ready while all actual invitations remain unsent pending the named recipient decision.
